fatal_errors: No supporting prior evidence or citations are provided.
The predicted 15–20% performance improvement and 25–30% PGM reduction are invented and unsupported by the target results.
The intervention is reduced to a generic computational design tool, omitting the closed-loop high-throughput synthesis, post-ageing screening, Bayesian optimisation, and inverse-analysis campaign.

The proposed mechanism emphasizes dispersion and sintering, whereas the target evidence primarily implicates ageing-induced electronic and atomic reconstruction, especially cooperative Cu–Pt adsorption sites and element-specific isolation of Pt.
Testing and ageing conditions are too vague to establish applicability or enable a controlled comparison with the reported catalyst system.
explanation: The response recognizes machine-learning-guided catalyst discovery and proposes an aged, head-to-head performance test, so it partially aligns with the central discovery concept. However, it does not reconstruct the actual automated closed-loop campaign, the five- to nineteen-element 1 wt% catalyst space on La-doped gamma-alumina, the severe cyclic 900 °C ageing protocol, or the specified near-stoichiometric multicomponent feed. Its generic dispersion/sintering mechanism misses the main Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction and hydrocarbon-assisted NO-reduction interpretation. The baseline is not operationally defined like the Pd/Al2O3 benchmark, and its numerical benefit and PGM-reduction claims are unsupported. The falsification experiment is directionally useful but relies on arbitrary thresholds and unspecified activity metrics, gas composition, ageing procedure, and statistical design.
